title: The Tannisho, part two
hook: read the later sections on faith and doubt
tomorrow: who sings his teachings from a cave, and why sing them at all?

segments.voice: Yesterday, a teacher with not one disciple, because the vow does the work: other power. This week's lines come back in today's round: what is empty, the diamond, like dew, no picking and choosing, the way is here, the moon in a dewdrop. Now, the worried student.

A beloved coach retires, and within a season the new staff are quoting him for things he never said. The fans who knew him wince. Yuien, the student who wrote down Shinran's sayings, felt that wince. After his teacher's death, he heard people teaching in Shinran's name things Shinran never taught. So he wrote it down, and the book's title says why: the Tannisho, notes lamenting the differences.
screen: `QUOTED FOR WHAT HE NEVER SAID.` → `YUIEN WINCES.` → `NOTES LAMENTING THE DIFFERENCES.`

segments.voice: In the later sections, Yuien takes the mistaken teachings one at a time. Some said you can't be born in the Pure Land unless you study the scriptures; Yuien answers that the nembutsu needs no learning. Some said the bigger your gifts to the temple, the bigger the Buddha you'd become; Yuien calls that baseless. Notice the pattern. Each mistake adds a condition: be learned enough, be generous enough, be sure enough. Then, near the end, a story. In Honen's circle, Shinran once said his entrusting and his teacher's were one and the same. Others objected: how could his match the master's? Honen settled it: my shinjin is given by Amida, and so is Shinran's, so they are one. And Yuien remembers Shinran saying that when he pondered the vow, it seemed made for him, Shinran, alone. Entrusted, in this record, means nothing added. No test to pass first, no amount of certainty to reach. Just the weight, set down.
screen: `NO LEARNING REQUIRED.` · `NO BIGGER BUDDHA FOR BIGGER GIFTS.` · `HONEN: OUR SHINJIN IS ONE.` · `NOTHING ADDED.` · then, large: `ENTRUSTED.`

segments.voice: Write one worry on a scrap of paper, in a few plain words. Fold it once and set it down somewhere out of reach, a shelf, a drawer, under a cup. For the rest of the sit, let your hands rest empty in your lap, until the bell.
The Tannisho, part two: Yuien's corrections, and the story of the shinjin that Honen and Shinran shared. Entrusting, with nothing added.
The line to take with you: entrusted, the worry still real and no longer carried alone. Eight of eleven, read.

screen: `DAY 1694 COUNTS.` → `THE MAHAYANA SOURCES, REREAD · 8 OF 11.` → `TOMORROW: WHO SINGS HIS TEACHINGS FROM A CAVE?`

howItsDone: In Shin Buddhist temples, the Tannisho is read and discussed, and the nembutsu is said as thanks; some teachers point to Yuien's corrections when explaining that the teaching adds no conditions.

fork.setup: your aunt hears a speaker say you have to study for years before your prayers 'count.' what would Yuien's corrections point to?
options: an added condition: his record says the nembutsu needs no learning.

fork.reveal: Yuien's later sections push back on each added condition: learning, bigger gifts, more certainty. entrusting adds nothing.

original.note: Japanese: notes (抄) lamenting (歎) differences (異), the title Yuien gave his record.

chat.meaning: In the Tannisho, entrusting adds no conditions, not even feeling sure. Mai's worry can stay real and still be set down.

tie.story: Yuien wrote down Shinran's sayings to clear away added conditions: entrusting needs no learning, no bigger gifts, no perfect certainty.
tie.friend: Mai's worry under Ông's juniper is still real; she just isn't carrying it alone while she waits.
tie.you: what worry could you set down, still real, for one day?

Yuien.meaning: Shinran's student, who wrote down the Tannisho

Honen.meaning: Shinran's teacher, who taught the nembutsu in Kyoto

shinjin.meaning: true entrusting, given by Amida in Shinran's teaching

Pure Land.meaning: Amida Buddha's realm, where those who trust the vow are born

nembutsu.meaning: saying Amida Buddha's name: Namu Amida Butsu
